title: Beethoven’s Fifth through the recording horn
work: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, Op. 67 — first movement
question: What changes in phrasing when acoustic pioneers and Mengelberg meet a modern orchestra?
intro: The Odeon recording’s Kark/1910 attribution is disputed by James Hepokoski’s research, which dates the recording to August 1911 and infers Künneke as its unnamed conductor; Nikisch’s November 1913 session is securely documented. Nikisch omits the exposition repeat, so his map begins at the modern reference’s repeated exposition, 1:42.6, rather than falsely equating the two complete durations. Mengelberg is represented by one unjoined disc side, with mapping limited to the shared exposition and its repeat. Acoustic recording balances and historic transfer speeds complicate claims about original orchestral tone or exact tempo.
